title: Research: offload heavy checks and the mechanics track from the M1 to cloud compute
description: Owner 2026-10-09 (verbatim excerpt): 'i wonder if we should rent a beefy server for a month so we can get faster CI ... look around for something that would significantly speed up our stuff and offload the processor intensive tasks from the macbook air m1 so the m1 can focus on ui polish things and mechanics stuff can have speedy cloud server'. Research brief: compare (a) faster hosted CI runners (GitHub larger runners, Blacksmith, Depot, Namespace, Ubicloud, BuildJet, and whatever 'useJog' refers to), (b) a rented dedicated/cloud box (Hetzner, OVH, AWS/GCP spot, etc.) used as a self-hosted runner and/or a remote dev box where mechanics-track agents run Claude Code + worktrees + bin/check_all.sh, (c) Claude Code cloud/remote sessions. Inputs: bin/check_all.sh, .githooks/pre-push, .github/workflows/*.yml, mise toolchain (Elixir/Erlang, Node, Playwright Chromium). Output: ranked recommendation with monthly cost, expected speed-up, setup effort, security (secrets, GitHub token scope), and what changes in our workflow. Read-only; no purchases, no sign-ups.
notes:
Result 2026-10-09: first pick rent a Linux box for the mechanics agents (Hetzner CCX43 hourly trial, then AX102 ~EUR257/mo); Jog (usejog.com) = cheap GitHub runners, <$5/mo, small vendor; Claude Code cloud sessions not ready (4 vCPU, no Erlang/Elixir, Node 22 only, gh pr blocked by proxy). Owner questions open: region, gate, Jog vendor trust, rental length.
Owner 2026-10-09: budget max $20/month; no Jog, use GitHub free hosted CI.

BRIEF (drafted 2026-10-08, PM-approved for assignment; developer Opus, designer consult for book-ui.md sentence, Opus review + second opinion because existing saves change behavior):
# Brief: loka-8mm — world time starts when the player first enters the world

Base: `main` 9acaf2b5. Beads: `loka-8mm`. Lane: **Hosted PR** (must merge alone; `bin/check_all.sh`
once, pre-push hook is the final run, ready PR, fresh reviewer once CI is green, merge per
WORKFLOW step 7). Developer: Opus. Lessons: `docs/lessons/mechanics.md` (check every committed
intermediate state with the real save loader), `docs/lessons/mobile.md`.

## Goal

The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): world time starts as soon as the player enters the
world for the first time. No time passes while the ancestry screen is shown. This reverses the
2026-10-06 ruling
(`docs/decisions/owner-decision-d11-prechoice-elapsed-2026-10-06.md`, "Allow elapsed updates").
Source: the question at `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-e2-gate-fable-audit.md:58-61`. Today
`stepElapsed` (`kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:167-180`) skips the ancestry gate that `step`
applies (`:126-131`). As a result, 2 minutes on the ancestry screen is 6000 units at rate 50.

## Decision: what "first entry into the world" is

First entry is the **accepted `choose_ancestry` decision**, which writes the `character.select`
row. The predicate is the existing `needsAncestry(world, actor)` at
`kernel/ts/src/commands/actions.ts:55-56`:
`!!world.cartridge.ancestries && !characterChoice(world, actor)`. It is the same condition that
`step` inlines at `world.ts:126-131` and that `refusal()` uses at `actions.ts:192-193`. On a
cartridge with no `ancestries`, first entry is world creation and the gate does nothing. The
ferry, scene, sampler and pre-v038 missing_child fixtures are therefore unchanged.

Room entry is not a separate event. The player is placed in the entry room at creation
(`mechanics.md:40-44`), and the ancestry choice is the first thing the player can do there.

## Required changes (smallest complete set)

1. **Kernel gate.** Export `needsAncestry` from `actions.ts`. In `step`, replace the inline
   condition with it (no behavior change). In `stepElapsed`, add
   `if (needsAncestry(world, world.character)) return reject('invalid_state');`. Put it after
   the validate, `identity` and command-id checks, so malformed or foreign elapsed commands keep
   their current codes, and before the owner/capability lookup. Every replay path inherits the
   gate with no extra code: `mobile/authority/local-story/delivery.ts:63`,
   `receipt-history.ts:35`, `kernel/ts/play/run.ts:74` and `kernel/ts/test/e1_case_host.ts:24`.
2. **Driver: no credit before the choice.** The kernel gate alone is not enough. The app ticks
   every 250 ms whenever it is active (`mobile/app/App.tsx:99-112`), and nothing checks
   ancestry (`elapsed.ts`, `delivery.ts`, `App.tsx`, `session.ts`, `invocation.ts`,
   `authority.ts`). With only the kernel gate:
   - every pulse on the ancestry screen would be rejected;
   - `ClockDriver.advance` would turn that rejection into a fault (`elapsed.ts:130-131`), and
     the Book would show "Time stopped: invalid_state" (`presenter.ts:48`, `Book.tsx:192`);
   - after the choice, the wall time spent on the ancestry screen would still be credited,
     because `capture` uses `mono - baseline` or `wall - old.wall_ms` (`elapsed.ts:107-111`).

   **Fix:** in `ClockDriver.capture` (`elapsed.ts:90-115`), set `d = 0` (the computation at `:107-111`) while
   `needsAncestry(this.s.world, this.s.world.character)` holds. `accounted(old, 0, rate, wall)`
   then re-anchors the wall clock and the monotonic baseline with no credit
   (`elapsed-store.ts:68-79`). The target stays at the head, so `drain` never delivers elapsed
   before the choice.

   The `choose_ancestry` invocation already reserves time through
   `driver.reserve` → `capture('active')` (`invocation.ts:91-95`). That capture happens before
   the choice commits, so it anchors the baseline at the moment of choice. Time credited after
   that starts exactly at the choice. No new state, timer or row is needed.
3. **Decision record.** Add `docs/decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md`.
   It records the owner answer marked (paraphrased), the predicate above, and the save impact
   below. Add one line to the 2026-10-06 record:
   `Superseded 2026-10-08 by [world time starts at entry](owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md).`
4. **Optional, only if it is one line:** the `payload.type !== 'elapsed'` exemption at
   `actions.ts:192` becomes unreachable, because `step` refuses elapsed at `world.ts:125`. Leave
   it unless deleting it is a one-token change that tests still cover.

## Spec amendment (spec first, same PR)

- **`docs/system/mechanics.md:303`.** Replace the paragraph with:
  > Under the [owner's world-time ruling](../decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md), world time starts when the player first enters the world: the accepted selection. Before selection, `stepElapsed` refuses trusted elapsed updates as `invalid_state`, as Step refuses ordinary commands, so the clock and due jobs stay at the birth clock. The local driver credits no wall time before selection; credited time starts at the selection invocation's reservation. This supersedes the [2026-10-06 pre-choice elapsed ruling](../decisions/owner-decision-d11-prechoice-elapsed-2026-10-06.md).
- **`mechanics.md:43-44`.** Change "precedes ordinary player commands, while trusted elapsed
  updates retain their separately authorized admission." to "precedes ordinary player commands
  and trusted elapsed updates; world time starts at selection."
- **`docs/system/save.md:229` (M1-A).** After "A new command passes `stepElapsed`", add
  "(which refuses `invalid_state` before [D11 selection](mechanics.md#d11-character-choice-selected-contract), matching Step)".
- **`save.md` "Durable elapsed sessions" (after `:236`).** Add: "Before D11 selection a capture
  re-anchors wall and monotonic evidence with zero credit; the target stays at the confirmed

## Save impact (pre-production rules: `owner-decision-forward-development-2026-10-05.md:7-16`)

The release pin is the cartridge `content_hash` (`authority.ts:92-99`), so this kernel change
does not change any pin. Existing chapter-one saves from older builds fall into three cases:

- **(a) Nearly every existing device save of chapter one has accepted pre-choice elapsed
  receipts.** The old driver delivered elapsed on every 250 ms active pulse while the ancestry
  screen was shown.
  - *Plain reopen:* opens cleanly. The clock it already committed stays as saved, with no
    rewrite. The driver credits nothing more until the choice.
  - *Reopen through `receiptHistory`* (`exchange-save.ts:25`, `liquid-save.ts:30`, used once
    exchange or liquid history exists): **every such save refuses**, and the label it shows
    says malformed or corrupt. The forward-development policy permits this, so it does not
    block. State it plainly in the PR body so the owner is not surprised to see "corrupt" on
    their own device save. The replay now rejects those receipts, so it throws
    `SyntaxError('malformed JSON: inconsistent accepted history')` (`receipt-history.ts:18-20`).
    This is an **explicit refusal**, never a silent change. The developer must confirm the
    host code it surfaces as (expected `save_corrupt`), state it in the PR, and add **no**
    compatibility code.
- **(b) Older save that closed with pending pre-choice debt** (checkpoint `target > clock`
  before selection). After the change, capture credits 0 but keeps the old target. `drain`
  then delivers, the kernel rejects it, and the Book shows "Time stopped: invalid_state".
  `reserve` drains the existing debt before any invocation, so `choose_ancestry` itself fails
  too. The only way out is Start over, which `Fault` offers for every fault
  (`Book.tsx:192`, `:229-238`). That is explicit, not silent. Record it in the PR.
  Do not clamp the target. Clamping would change a save, and it would add machinery that
  exists only for old data.
- **(c) New saves:** no pre-choice receipts or debt exist.

Under the user's rule, a second-opinion review is needed only if save or reconcile behavior
changes. Reopen of old saves does change, by refusing case (a), so **add the second opinion**.

## Designer

**Consult.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md:231` says a slice that changes what the player sees consults the
designer for its brief, its Book UI spec text and its review. This slice changes what the player
sees in two small ways:

- "Catching up…" (`Book.tsx:191`) no longer appears on the ancestry screen.
- The first time shown after the choice is the chapter start time, not start plus dwell time.

No new element, wording or layout is added. The designer's scope is small:

- write the `book-ui.md:458` sentence;
- confirm that no design-system change is needed;
- review the UI-visible behavior in the PR.

## Scope trigger (stop and ask)

- Any change to the save format, the checkpoint row shape, a protocol or GameView shape, or the
  ErrorCode set.
- `kernel_api` in `INSTALLED`: do not bump it. No documented bump rule exists, and recent bumps
  came with new capabilities (`git log -S"kernel_api: '1.3"`). If a check demands a bump, stop
  and ask.
- Any need for a migration, a clamp or compatibility code for old saves.
- Any E1 case that falls below 38/38 and cannot be explained by this rule.

## Process rules (copy)

- Self-review is ONE pass: `/code-review medium`.
- Narrow mutant runs only (the two red controls). Full-suite mutation sweeps happen only before
  a release (owner rule).
- Run long commands in the background, without polling.
- Review: one fresh Opus reviewer, plus a second opinion (save reopen behavior changes for old
  saves).
- Ponytail before implementation and Ponytail Review before handoff.

## Out of scope

- New UI elements, a clock on the ancestry screen, migrating old saves, and the `actions.ts:192`
  cleanup beyond one token.

6. Owner OK 2026-10-08 (paraphrased) — efficient mutant sweeps:
   a. `bin/mutate.sh`: input = a mutant list (file, line or exact old text, replacement) + a test command; for each: save a copy, apply, run the tests, restore from the copy, record red/green; print one summary table; exit non-zero if the restore leaves any diff. Small POSIX sh; red control in a throwaway repo (break restore -> check fails; break apply -> check fails).
   b. Narrow first: run each mutant against the test files that import the mutated module; full suite only for survivors.
   c. Briefs/agents: long commands run with run_in_background and wait for the completion notice; no sleep/poll loops. One line in developer.md, reviewer.md and WORKFLOW token hygiene.
   d. An agent past ~220k tokens hands remaining work to a fresh agent with a short brief (extend the fix-round rule to long sweeps).
   Decision record line (same record style as agent-tooling 2026-10-08).
7. Owner 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): long mutant runs only before a product release, and always announced to the owner first. Rule (WORKFLOW token hygiene + developer.md + reviewer.md + docs/lessons/checks.md one line + decision record): FULL-suite mutant sweeps run only at release-candidate certification and the E3 gate on that same candidate (E2's planted-defect claim is already done). Everything else: red control on the new test only, and "already caught?" triage against the test files that import the mutated module; reviewers sample 2-3 narrow mutants. Schema fixture sweeps (lessons/contracts.md) stay: they rerun fixtures only and are short. Any agent that expects a run over ~10 min (full-suite mutants, the 10,000-sequence simulator) stops and asks the PM, who tells the owner before it starts.

Gate checklist docs/briefs/chapter-one/chapter-one-e2-gate-checklist-2026-10-08.md:34: deer remark says 'no cap assertion I could find'; kernel/ts/test/deer.test.ts:461-474 checks deer member count (3 slots) over thirty days; say 'not measured against the cap mutant' (PR #321 round-2 optional note).

WORKFLOW token hygiene / handoff: whenever the PM writes the continuation handoff (owner asks to clear early, or session end), it also writes up to 5 evidence-backed improvement candidates as Beads issues labeled housekeeping (evidence: run id, token count, file:line; expected saving). 10. Instead a pattern retro at each milestone gate (E3, RC certification, release): a Sonnet subagent reads the housekeeping issues, review records and gh CI timings since the last gate and proposes at most 5 cross-session items; add a line to the gate checklist template.

description: Owner 2026-10-09 (verbatim): 'can you get fable to audit the proposed 2 lane workflow with github free CI, to optimize for speed of development since we are in preproduction, and less damage on my personal m1 processor'. Read-only Fable audit of the two-lane workflow: polish lane on the M1 (Storybook live sessions, local pre-push hook, two-check-runner cap) and mechanics lane (toolbox/* branches, focused local tests, hook skip per #341 loka-kgd.4, review per item, ci.yml + book-e2e.yml dispatched per batch head on free GitHub runners; repo is public so minutes are unlimited). notes: Audit result 2026-10-09 (Fable): (1) hosted CI gate for all branches, pre-push hook no-op; (2) CI on push to non-main branches, concurrency cancels; (3) ci.yml 8->~4 min: split typescript job, e1-recorder nightly/dispatch only, npm cache; (4) book-e2e split e2e/storybook jobs; (5) developers focused tests only + gh run watch; (6) polish PR review as PR comments, no records (keep for save/protocol/kernel contract slices); (7) agent cap -> load check (uptime <8), 3-4 agents; (8) keep pre-commit. DESIGN INPUT (commit as docs/briefs/polish/design-input-p1-2026-10-09.md): # Design input: batch P1, Loka picker + polish panel (Beads loka-x6t.3)

Developer tool inside Storybook, not Book UI. Owner words and PM rulings: Beads loka-x6t,
loka-x6t.3; lane: [live polish session](../../WORKFLOW.md#live-polish-session).

## Separation rule

- The addon never imports `mobile/app/book/tokens.ts` or any `book/` module, and never adds a
  node to the story's layout: the preview overlay is `position: fixed`, max z-index,
  `pointer-events: none` except while picking. The Tidewave 74 px strip goes with Tidewave;
  stories get `100vh` back.
- Manager side (panel, toolbar) uses only `storybook/theming` roles (`theme.color.secondary`,
  `.positive`, `.warning`, `.negative`, `theme.textMutedColor`, `theme.appBorderColor`,
  `theme.background.app`, `theme.typography.size.s1/s2`, `.fonts.mono`). `manager.ts` already
  maps the base roles to the Book's light palette; positive/warning/negative stay Storybook's
  defaults, so status colour reads as tool, not page.
- Preview side (overlay) has no theme; it uses two plain values: `#1EA7FD` (Storybook blue,
  separate from every Book palette) and `#FFFFFF`. No other raw colour in the addon.

## 1. Picker overlay (preview iframe)

- **On/off.** Toolbar TOOL button "Pick" (crosshair icon, active state = `barSelectedColor`,
  like the viewport tool); key `P` (unused by Storybook; the preview forwards keydown).
  Turning Pick on opens the Polish panel if hidden. `Esc` clears the pending pick; a second
  `Esc` (nothing pending) turns Pick off. Pick stays on after a submit.
- **While picking** a transparent capture layer takes every pointer event: no click reaches
  the story (a tap would turn the page). Pick off = Storybook as today.
- **Hover.** Outline `2px solid #1EA7FD` at 60 % alpha, no fill, on the hovered element's
  border box (`getBoundingClientRect`, rounded). Label chip, 11 px `ui-monospace`, white on
  `#1EA7FD`, padding 2 px 6 px, radius 2 px, placed above the box's top-left (flipped to below
  when the box top < 20 px; clamped inside the 414 px viewport): `EntityLine › Tap · 382×28`.
  The chain is the React dev fiber owner chain, named components only (RNW `View`/`Text`/
  `Pressable` and Storybook decorators dropped), root-most first, at most 4 deep.
- **Click** pins the element: outline 2px solid 100 %, fill `#1EA7FD` at 12 %, chip gains the
  pick number `1`. **Shift-click** adds up to 4 elements (`2`..`4`); plain click replaces.
  Click on a pinned element unpins it.
- **No note box in the iframe.** The composer lives in the panel (section 2), which is full
  height beside a 414 px story, so nothing ever covers the picked element and a tall pick
  (whole Page) still works; the manager focuses the textarea on pick. The pinned outline stays
  until send or `Esc`.
- **Keys in the composer.** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` sends; `Enter` is a newline; `Esc` clears the
  pending pick and text. An element is optional: a feel request ("make it calmer") is text only.

## 2. Polish panel (manager addon panel, `panelPosition: 'right'`)

Set in `manager.ts`; Storybook keeps the owner's dragged width (no API for it). Tab title
`Polish`, with ` · n working` while n > 0. One column, top to bottom:

- **Header (sticky, 40 px).** Left: session pill, 12 px: green dot + branch name
  (`polish/2026-10-09`) when `bin/polish_session.sh` serves a session; grey dot + "No session ·
  picks go to Beads" otherwise. Right: **Close batch**, outline button 28 px high, only while a
  session runs. Click = inline confirm in the same row: "Close batch · 7 items?  Close  Cancel";
  disabled while any item is `working` (`polish_session.sh close` refuses a dirty tree).
- **Conversation (scrolls; newest at bottom; autoscroll only when already at bottom).**
  - Owner item: 3 px left rule in `theme.color.secondary`, padding 8 px 10 px.
    Row 1: element chip(s) (mono 12 px, `appBorderColor` border, 24×24 thumbnail at left) +
    story title in muted 12 px. Row 2: prompt, 14 px. Row 3 (12 px muted): status dot + word ·
    model badge · summary · short sha (mono). Clicking a chip re-pins that element in the
    composer (a follow-up). Clicking the thumbnail toggles the full crop at panel width.
  - Status words and dots: `received` hollow grey; `working` pulsing `secondary`; `done`
    `positive` + one-line summary + `abc1234`; `Beads loka-xxx` `warning` + reason;
    `stopped` `negative` + reason (agent could not, PM note). Model badge: `SONNET` / `FABLE`,
    10 px uppercase, 1 px border, no fill; shown from `working` on (the PM routes first).
  - PM message: full-width card, 1 px `warning` border, label `PM` in muted small caps, text
    ("suggest closing: review load is at 12 items"), buttons **Close batch** (opens the same
    inline confirm) and **Keep going** (dismisses). Any other PM note: same card with
    `appBorderColor`, no buttons.
  - Empty state (session running, no items), centred muted 12 px: "Press P or Pick, then click
    anything in the story. Shift-click adds elements. Type a feel request without picking."
  - No session: same list; new items show `queued for Beads`, then `Beads loka-xxx` after
    `/polish-intake`. Composer stays usable.
- **Composer (sticky bottom).** Pending chips row (each with ×), textarea 3 rows growing to 8,
  hint line 11 px muted "⌘↩ send · esc clear · ⇧click adds an element", **Send** button
  (primary). `fable:` / `quick:` are typed prefixes; no control for them.

## 3. Payload

| Owner sees in the item | Sent to the agent (queue JSON) only |
|---|---|
| prompt; element chain; W×H; thumbnail; story title; `light · iPhone 11` | note, pick id, time; story id; palette; viewport name + size; per element: chain, box (x y w h), computed padding/margin/font-family/size/line-height/colour/background, `innerText` (≤ 200 chars), accessible role + name, `data-testid` if any; crop PNG path (box + 24 px, device pixel ratio 2) |

The owner never sees computed styles or JSON; a `Copy JSON` affordance is not needed.

## Proposed checks (developer slice)

- ast-grep: no `import` from `book/` under the addon directory.
- Overlay off: the story's `#storybook-root` boxes are identical with the addon loaded and
  not (one smoke assertion).
- Raw colour literals in the addon: exactly the two overlay constants; the manager files use
  theme roles only.

## For the owner

1. Composer in the panel, not a floating note box over the story (so a pick never gets
   covered). OK?
2. `P` as the Pick key; `Esc` twice to leave Pick.
3. Close batch disabled while an item is `working` (PM can still close by hand).
4. Screenshot: if the in-page crop needs a small dependency (html-to-image), take it; a
   server-side re-render would not match a Live story.

title: Retro (E2 gate): items 1-4 approved, item 5 rejected
description:
Pattern retro after the E2 gate (2026-10-08, Sonnet, read-only). PROPOSED — awaiting owner approval; on approval move approved items into the next housekeeping batch, close rejected ones with a reason. PM recommendation: approve 1-4, reject 5.

# E2 gate pattern retro (2026-10-08)

1. Review findings are prose claims, not code (conf. high). Of ~14 findings in e2-s0..s5 records, 0 blockers and ~12 are overclaimed coverage or wrong citations: s2 nit1-2 (:233-236, reward_storage cite), s3 nit1-2 (r9c_elapsed_jobs.test.ts:213, :297-305), s4 should-fix 1-2 (header :257-259; PR table vs transcripts.test.ts:24), s5 nit1 (r9c_faults.test.ts:5), nit2 (README:117 line cite), gate nit (checklist:34), round-2 note. Every slice S2-S5 needed a fix round. Saving ~100-300k tokens/slice. Fix: developer.md rule: a "catches/only here/every" claim or file:line cite must be copied from a red-control or grep run in the same turn and listed in the PR body; reviewer samples 2.
2. Nit fix loops chain re-checks (conf. high). #321: 18 commits, 8 review-record commits, 5 review passes (Opus, Fable, Opus re-check x2) for 2 doc nits; the round-1 nit fix introduced a new wrong claim (second-opinion:35, "F4 is wrong"). Saving ~150k tokens + 2-3 CI runs per slice. Fix: WORKFLOW review section: comment/doc-only nits are batched or dropped, no re-review agent; PM checks the diff is comment-only.
3. docs/reviews/README.md index is a shared append point (conf. high). 3 of 4 main-merges on S1-S4 touched it on both sides (db10c963, 93fa596c, c913b0c0); each merge or record commit makes a new head. Cancelled PR-branch runs: s5 4, s0 4, s1 2; 12 of 48 main runs cancelled. Saving: ~1 merge and 1-2 CI runs per PR. Fix: delete the index (let check_docs glob docs/reviews) or have records land on the housekeeping branch.
4. Test-only TS diffs take the full pre-push lane (conf. medium). bin/ci_scope.sh treats mobile/authority/local-story and kernel/ts/test as "code", so check_all.sh runs mix test and credo (CI elixir job 65-93s, run 37808875291). Contributes to the load 50-152 timeouts. Fix: in pre-push, skip the Elixir half when the diff is only *.test.ts, kernel/ts/test or docs; cartridge/oracle paths stay full.
5. Draft PRs show a red check (conf. low, noise). ci-green runs `exit 1` when all jobs are skipped: 6 failures, ~3s each (37818225834, 37820341523, 37828128147, 37831054177). Cost is PM confusion, not compute. Fix: ci-green passes on draft when needs are skipped.

PM note on item 5: REJECT — the red ci-green on draft runs is the #315 safety feature (a skipped-everything draft run must not look green to auto-merge).
notes: Owner 2026-10-08: APPROVED items 1-4 (claims and file:line cites backed by a same-turn check and listed in the PR body; comment/doc-only nit fixes verified by the PM without a re-review agent; generate docs/reviews/README.md from record files (keep the one-line verdict from each record's first line); skip the Elixir half of pre-push for TS-test/docs-only diffs, hosted CI unchanged). REJECTED item 5: the red ci-green on draft runs is the #315 safety feature. Next: implement 1-4 in the next housekeeping batch.
